gaps.quote: is an explicit permutation $L$ of record addresses
gaps.note: The page calls L a permutation without saying what a permutation is, and the reader profile does not cover it.
The suffix of a record's polynomial is never explained, so the reader cannot tell which coefficients or bits it refers to.

gaps.quote: It places the selected bits of all participating axes at one common offset
gaps.note: The page never defines a selected bit or says how the bits are selected; the reader can only guess that it is the bit a butterfly acts on.

gaps.quote: Each axis's part outside the prefix Number each axis's chunks from the highest down
gaps.note: The sentence is broken, and it does not say which chunks of an axis lie outside the prefix, so the chunk index cannot be assigned as described.

gaps.term: grouping by chunk index gives a common offset
gaps.quote: Each such group carries the selected bits at one common offset
gaps.note: This is asserted, not derived; the page does not show why grouping chunks with the same index puts the selected bits at one common offset.

gaps.quote: Every single-bit move and chunk exchange, in building $L$ and in restoring the order, is counted in the bound.
gaps.note: The page does not show what the bound counts, so the claim that every move is included cannot be checked from this page.

gaps.term: pointwise multiplication commutes with the layout
gaps.quote: pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation $L$ to both operands
gaps.note: This is asserted without proof or a pointer, so the reader cannot check that permuting records commutes with pointwise multiplication.

gaps.term: one pass per axis without the shape
gaps.quote: Without this shape, a round would need one pass per axis.
gaps.note: The claim about the cost of a round without this shape is not justified on the page.
